surfaces.part: goods hanging in the alcove (bags, garments)

answer.evidence: Rows 1-4 form a light top band. Row 1 is a mid-tone, rows 2-3 are light, and row 4 is the lightest and acts as the front-edge line. Row 5 is a dark eave shadow, so the band is a real top surface rather than a front-facing strip, similar to the green cabinet reference. Below it the alcove (rows 6-20) and the drawer front (rows 25-28) form a front face of about 25 rows. The inner shelf ledge at rows 21-22 has its own edge line and shadow at rows 23-24. No receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a wall shelf/cabinet with a cream back panel, wood frame and small bottles/items. Measured facts: 20 visible tones per tile (equal to well-roofed at 20, above stall-cheese at 17), 3% near-flat coverage (below stall at 13%), and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted brown rather than near-black. By the numbers it matches the references. By eye, though, the cream back panel is a large, smooth area with only a faint gradient and little grain, and the wood frame has about 3-4 steps against 5-6 on the stall and well. The small bottles add some variety. The piece is clean and in style, but its shading is shallower and its surfaces plainer than the richer references, so it falls slightly short.

surfaces.part: inner shelf ledge above the drawers
hanging accessories (bags, scarves, ties) on the back panel

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a constant 32 px wide on every row, so the object is a plain rectangle with no side face. At the top, rows 1-4 form a tan band that gets lighter toward the bottom. Row 4 (#f7d5a2) is the lightest and acts as the front-edge line, and row 5 (#805434) is a dark eave shadow below it. That gives a top surface of about 4 rows, similar to the green cabinet and bookshelf references. Below it, rows 6-22 hold the open shelf interior with hanging accessories, and rows 21-22 form a light shelf ledge with a dark shadow in rows 23-24. Rows 25-28 are the drawer fronts with handles, and rows 29-31 are the base and ground shadow. The front face runs about rows 6-30, roughly 25 rows. The top band is thin but has a front-edge line and an eave shadow, so it is more than a bare rim.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a wall cabinet with shelves, bottles and drawers, so it is the same kind as the furniture and stall references. It measures 20 visible tones per 16x16 tile, level with the well (20) and above the stall (17) and hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 3%, below the stall's 13%, so the cream back panel is not a large flat fill. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted and reads as a dark brown wood tone rather than a black sticker line. The frame has about 4-5 wood steps with highlight edges and the shelf contents are varied, though the grain is a little less developed than the stall or well. A careful artist would accept it beside the references without it looking thinner or flatter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a wall display shelf with a cream/beige frame and a light interior holding small coloured items. Measured facts: 20 visible tones per tile, 3% near-flat coverage, 0% neutral dark edges. That matches prop-well-roofed (20 tones) and exceeds prop-stall-cheese (17 tones, 13% flat), so the numbers do not mark it as shallow. The outline is tinted brown, in the dark-material-tone style rather than a black sticker line. By eye, though, the frame and shelf boards use only about 3-4 lightness steps, with few per-plank grain dots or highlights. The back panel looks fairly smooth compared with the stall's textured awning and goods. The small items give some variety, but the piece is quieter and flatter than the best references. The numbers are on par; the eye sees a slightly thinner ramp and less grain.

answer.evidence: The top band at rows 1-4 is light tan, with a brighter highlight on row 4 as a front-edge line and a dark brown eave shadow on row 5.
